cpu.desc: CPU allocation in threads. 100% = 1 thread, 200% = 2 threads

disk.desc: Disk space allocation in MB (4096 MB = 4 GB)

memory.desc: How much memory in MB to allocate

ip.desc: What IP to bind the server to

port.desc: Game port (UDP) for Direct Connect. Not used when Direct Connect is off

directconnect.desc: Players join with IP, port and password (needed for crossplay with Epic, GOG and Microsoft Store). Off means Steam relay: players join with the Game ID instead and no port is opened

serverpassword.desc: Password for Direct Connect, up to 28 characters. If empty the game makes up a random one and writes it to GameInfo.txt

worldindex.desc: World save slot to load or create (0 to 29)

worldseed.desc: Seed for a new world. 0 picks a random seed

worldmode.desc: Mode used when a new world is created

gameid.desc: Fixed Game ID for Steam relay joins (alphanumeric, 28 characters). Empty keeps the one the game generates

#!/bin/bash
# Core Keeper launcher, written by Aether Panel before every start (edits are overwritten).
# The settings arrive from the panel as CK_* environment variables.
LOG=logs/CoreKeeperServer.log
mkdir -p logs gamedata
rm -f GameID.txt GameInfo.txt
: > "$LOG"

set -- -batchmode -logfile "$LOG" -datapath gamedata -world "$CK_WORLD" -worldname "$CK_NAME" -worldseed "$CK_SEED" -worldmode "$CK_MODE" -maxplayers "$CK_MAXPLAYERS"
if [ -n "$CK_GAMEID" ]; then set -- "$@" -gameid "$CK_GAMEID"; fi
if [ "$CK_DIRECT" = "true" ]; then
  set -- "$@" -ip "$CK_IP" -port "$CK_PORT"
  if [ -n "$CK_PASSWORD" ]; then set -- "$@" -password "$CK_PASSWORD"; fi
fi

# The Linux server needs an X display even in batch mode, so give it a virtual one.
if ! command -v Xvfb >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Xvfb is missing: the Core Keeper server needs it (Debian/Ubuntu: apt install xvfb libxi6)."
  exit 1
fi
DISP=$(( CK_PORT % 50000 + 100 ))
rm -f "/tmp/.X$DISP-lock"
Xvfb ":$DISP" -screen 0 1x1x24 -ac -nolisten tcp -nolisten unix >/dev/null 2>&1 &
XVFB=$!
export DISPLAY=":$DISP"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$PWD/.steam/sdk64:$PWD/linux64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH"
sleep 1

./CoreKeeperServer "$@" &
CK=$!
tail -n +1 -F "$LOG" 2>/dev/null &
TAIL=$!

# Stopping from the panel sends SIGINT to this script. Background jobs of a script ignore
# SIGINT, so pass it on as SIGTERM, which the server handles by saving and exiting.
trap 'kill -TERM $CK 2>/dev/null' INT TERM
CODE=0
while kill -0 $CK 2>/dev/null; do
  wait $CK
  CODE=$?
done
sleep 1
kill $TAIL $XVFB 2>/dev/null
exit $CODE
